exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Credentials In Files
exploitedBy.relevance: Directly describes adversaries finding credentials stored in plaintext within configuration files.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Unsecured Credentials
exploitedBy.relevance: Parent technique covering the broader risk of secrets stored without encryption in accessible locations.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Software Deployment Tools
exploitedBy.relevance: Unauthenticated access to a configuration agent API can allow adversaries to abuse deployment tools to execute commands across managed systems.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Cloud Administration Command
exploitedBy.relevance: Attackers can leverage unauthenticated agent APIs to issue administrative commands similar to cloud administration command abuse.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Valid Accounts
exploitedBy.relevance: Overprivileged service accounts represent valid accounts that adversaries can compromise and abuse for broad access.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Code Signing Policy Modification
exploitedBy.relevance: Lack of signature verification on configuration content mirrors the risk exploited when code signing policies are bypassed or absent.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exfiltration Over Unencrypted Non-C2 Protocol
exploitedBy.relevance: Unencrypted transport exposes configuration data to interception, analogous to data exfiltration over unencrypted protocols.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Non-Application Layer Protocol
exploitedBy.relevance: Use of unencrypted or non-standard protocols for configuration server communication enables traffic interception and manipulation.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Disable or Modify Tools
exploitedBy.relevance: Configuration drift can result from adversaries disabling or modifying security and configuration management tools without detection.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Patch System Image
exploitedBy.relevance: Undetected configuration drift may mask unauthorized modifications to system images or configurations by adversaries.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: File and Directory Discovery
exploitedBy.relevance: Adversaries use file and directory discovery to locate world-readable configuration state files containing sensitive information.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Disable or Modify Cloud Logs
exploitedBy.relevance: Insufficient logging of configuration changes mirrors the technique of disabling or modifying logs to evade detection.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Indicator Removal
exploitedBy.relevance: Without adequate logging, adversaries can make configuration changes and remove indicators of compromise without detection.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exploitation of Remote Services
exploitedBy.relevance: Unpatched configuration management agents expose known vulnerabilities that adversaries can exploit as remote services.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
exploitedBy.relevance: Configuration management agents exposed to the network represent public-facing applications exploitable via unpatched vulnerabilities.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
exploitedBy.relevance: Loading modules or plugins from untrusted sources directly maps to supply chain compromise of software dependencies.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Non-Standard Port
exploitedBy.relevance: Configuration agents listening on exposed ports can be targeted by adversaries probing non-standard ports for attack surfaces.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Boundary Bridging
exploitedBy.relevance: Excessive network exposure of agent listeners can allow adversaries to bridge network boundaries and access otherwise isolated systems.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Steal or Forge Authentication Certificates
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak host identity verification enables adversaries to forge or steal certificates to impersonate legitimate hosts to the configuration server.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Install Digital Certificate
exploitedBy.relevance: Adversaries can install fraudulent digital certificates to pass weak host identity checks by the configuration server.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Application or System Exploitation
exploitedBy.relevance: Without rollback, failed or malicious deployments can leave systems in a degraded or exploitable state indefinitely.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Shell History
exploitedBy.relevance: Environment variables containing secrets in deployment contexts can leak through shell history, exposing credentials to adversaries.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Modify Cloud Compute Configurations
exploitedBy.relevance: Lack of idempotency can result in partial or inconsistent configuration states that adversaries can exploit by manipulating cloud compute configurations.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Event Triggered Execution
exploitedBy.relevance: Partial configuration states from non-idempotent deployments may create unintended event triggers that adversaries can abuse for persistent execution.
